description: rates.html has substantial raw prose (ratio stays above the 0.30 D-RENDER-01 threshold) but the one load-bearing fact -- the actual rate -- exists only in a client-side script.

expected_false_negative.check: D-RENDER-02 (render-only facts, the check designed for exactly this)
expected_false_negative.why: Unreachable for one reason only: D-RENDER-02 hard-gates on a PROBE observation (`if not probe: continue` in skills/crawl-render-audit/scripts/detect_render.py), and lib/site_observer/probe.py::detect_capability() returns {'available': False, 'reason': 'MODEL_UNAVAILABLE'} unconditionally, so PROBE observations never exist through the real pipeline regardless of fixture content. The audit now reports this explicitly: run_audit emits an X-COV-01 coverage entry with reason UNAVAILABLE_INSTRUMENT naming D-RENDER-02, so the check reads as not-evaluable rather than as evaluated-and-passed. CORRECTION (supersedes an earlier note here): a previous version of this field claimed a second, more fundamental cause -- that run_audit.py::_invoke_detectors() never called detect_render()/detect_extract(). That orchestrator gap was real when written and has since been fixed; _invoke_detectors() calls both today (run_audit.py, the detect_render.detect_render and detect_extract.detect_extract lines). The other D-RENDER and D-EXTRACT checks do run end to end -- D-RENDER-01 fires from a full run_audit() on the js-render-gap fixture, and D-EXTRACT-02/04 on others. The claim of an orchestrator bug is withdrawn; only the probe gap remains.

notes: Deliberately distinct from js-render-gap: isolates the case D-RENDER-01's bulk-ratio heuristic cannot catch -- a single critical fact hidden in an otherwise text-heavy page.
